items.stem: Why does strong front-end loading (FEL) matter most before major spend is committed?

options.text: Early scope definition is cheap to change and prevents costly late rework
options.rationale: Correct: changes are far cheaper early; good FEL reduces overruns once construction starts.

options.text: It speeds construction by skipping design reviews
options.rationale: FEL adds rigorous early definition, it does not skip reviews.
FEL reduces but cannot eliminate risk.

options.text: It is only paperwork for regulators
options.rationale: FEL is core project discipline, not mere compliance paperwork.

items.explanation: Correct: changes are far cheaper early; good FEL reduces overruns once construction starts.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk that EPC-to-operations interfaces fail? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Involve operations in design reviews for operability
options.rationale: Correct: early operations input catches operability problems while they are cheap to fix.

options.text: Define interface responsibilities in a clear RACI matrix
options.rationale: Correct: explicit ownership prevents gaps at handover points.

options.text: Leave interface issues to be resolved at commissioning
options.rationale: Deferring interfaces to commissioning is when they become expensive failures.

options.text: Assume each contractor will manage shared boundaries alone
options.rationale: Unmanaged shared boundaries are exactly where interfaces fail.

items.explanation: Correct: early operations input catches operability problems while they are cheap to fix.

items.stem: A very early, order-of-magnitude (Class 5) cost estimate is presented. How should it be treated?

options.text: As a wide-range screening figure, not a firm budget
options.rationale: Correct: Class 5 estimates have large uncertainty and are for screening, with contingency applied.
Committing to a Class 5 number ignores its large uncertainty.

options.text: As more accurate than a Class 1 estimate
options.rationale: Class 1 is the most accurate; Class 5 is the least.
Early estimates need the largest contingency, not none.

items.explanation: Correct: Class 5 estimates have large uncertainty and are for screening, with contingency applied.
